entities.summary:
Uberto Gambara (1489–1549) was an Italian Roman Catholic bishop of Tortona and cardinal, serving the popes as nuncio in Portugal and later in England at the court of Henry VIII of England.

As a key figure in the Catholic Church during the tumultuous 16th century, Gambara played a crucial role in shaping the religious landscape of Europe. His diplomatic efforts and negotiations with European monarchs, particularly Henry VIII, contributed significantly to the Protestant Reformation and the establishment of the Church of England.


Uberto Gambara's legacy extends beyond his own lifetime, influencing the development of the Catholic Church and European politics. His experiences as nuncio in Portugal and England provide valuable insights into the complex relationships between the Church and secular power during this period.


The exact date of Uberto Gambara's death is not certain, but he was buried in the Cathedral of Tortona, where many other notable Italian bishops and cardinals are entombed. Despite the passing of centuries, Gambara's contributions to the Catholic Church and European history remain an important part of our understanding of the 16th century.
